coordination.notes: Branched from origin/backend/b0-expedition-state at cb4f57e. B7's claim recorded the gap this card closes and chose the external `habitat.` prefix as a stopgap; that prefix leaves intentionallyExternalPrefixes here, and `skill.enemy.` is now the only entry left. godot-rust/src/battle.rs, expedition.rs and strategy/ were NOT touched -- lanes A7 and S16 hold them. In habitat.rs only the test module is appended to; no fixture value, type or function was restructured, so the registry side of the equality test is B7-era code unchanged. THE ONE STRING THIS PASS LEAVES BEHIND: the vertical-slice battle fixture in battle.rs (and its mirrors in protocol.rs, mock_simulation_port.gd and five game/tests suites) still spells its hostile `ActorId("enemy.raptor.razorbeak.prototype")`. That is a battle *instance* ID in a hand-built fixture, not a creature definition ID: nothing resolves it against content (the encounter record's hostileActorIds is read only by the validator, and no GDScript looks a creature record up by ID -- paper dolls resolve by their own presentation.paper_doll.* id and battle_3d_staging.gd keys on the bridge's actor id), so renaming content did not break it and renaming it would have meant editing battle.rs, which this lane may not. Whoever lands A7 should rename those literals to enemy.raptor.razorbeak and the divergence is gone.
